props.title: The Piano
props.initialSlug: Period drama about a mute pianist

sections.content: The Piano (1993) stands as Jane Campion's masterpiece of repressed Victorian sexuality and feminine expression. Set in 1850s New Zealand, the film's mute protagonist Ada McGrath uses her piano to communicate when words fail, creating a powerful metaphor for female voice in patriarchal society. Campion's direction influenced later female-driven period pieces like Portrait of a Lady (1996) and Bright Star (2009), establishing a new visual language for depicting women's interior lives. The film's raw eroticism and psychological complexity earned Holly Hunter an Oscar for her wordless performance.

sections.content: The film's exploration of colonialism and cultural clash resonates with other New Zealand classics like Whale Rider (2002) and Once Were Warriors (1994). Campion's portrayal of the Maori people, while still through a Western lens, attempted more complexity than previous colonial narratives. The muddy, rain-soaked landscapes shot by Stuart Dryburgh created a template for depicting New Zealand's primal beauty, later echoed in The Lord of the Rings (2001-2003) trilogy.

The erotic tension between Harvey Keitel's Baines and Hunter's Ada influenced later period romances like The English Patient (1996) and The Age of Innocence (1993). Campion's focus on female desire and agency challenged conventional costume drama tropes. The piano itself becomes a character, its music (composed by Michael Nyman) expressing Ada's passionate inner life in ways that influenced scores like Atonement (2007) and The Hours (2002). sections.content: Campion's success with The Piano helped pave the way for other female directors tackling complex period pieces, from Sofia Coppola's Marie Antoinette (2006) to Céline Sciamma's Portrait of a Lady on Fire (2019). The film's unflinching examination of female sexuality and power dynamics influenced contemporary directors like Andrea Arnold (Wuthering Heights (2011)) and Lynne Ramsay (Ratcatcher (1999)).
